note: Judges the MUST only: RFC 8210 Section 8.3, 'If there are no more-preferred caches, it MUST issue a Reset Query and get an entire new load from the cache.' TestRTRCacheResetReloadsTheWholeSet and TestCacheResetTriggersResetQuery are byte-identical to the last judgement (one-session group: Reset, Serial, Reset after the Cache Reset; the new VRP Valid and the old NotFound; negative keeps Serial Queries and merges a delta). New unit TestCacheGroupCacheResetFromPreferredReloadsIt adds the two-cache case through startSessions, where the cache sending Cache Reset is the most preferred: positive asserts its query sequence Reset, Serial, Reset in the same round (load in rtr_session.go issues the second syncOnce), that the reload's 192.0.3.0/24 becomes Valid and the reset set's 192.0.2.0/24 becomes NotFound, so the new load replaces rather than merges; negative asserts the preference 20 cache receives no query and its VRP never validates. The pre-fix poll, which treated Cache Reset as a failure and moved to the less-preferred cache, fails both (no third preferred query, a standby query). Revert record on load exists.
